setup.title: Understeer on exit
setup.detail: Try less power-side diff locking or a softer front anti-roll bar. Driving fix: get the car rotated before you go to full throttle.

setup.title: RL: inside only 1.9°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RR: inside only -0.1°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: Rears running 11.3°C hotter
setup.detail: Rears are overworked: wheelspin or oversteer. Smoother throttle and the exit-oversteer fixes help.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 5 of 5 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T2, T3, T4, T5. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 5 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 79.1% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

cons.title: Coasting: 9.4% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 165 m per lap in T1, T3, T4, T5. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 3 corners
cons.detail: In T1, T2, T4 ABS is active for 82% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 1 corners
cons.detail: T3. Your rear tyres run 11°C hotter than the fronts, which is a symptom. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T1, T2)
cons.detail: T1: 2.9 m wider than your best lap; T2: 0.9 m wider than your best lap. Missing the apex makes the corner longer and slower.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Not using all the road on exit (T1, T2)
cons.detail: T1: about 7.7 m more was available; T2: about 3.2 m more was available. Using the full width lets you straighten the wheel and get on the throttle sooner.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T5, T4, T3, T2
cons.detail: T5: 0.42 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.35 s between your average and best pass; T3: 0.32 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.26 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T3, T1.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit the brake hard first, and the moment ABS starts working, ease off 5-10% instead of holding the pedal down.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T1, T2, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T2: ABS active 82% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T3: ABS active 66% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T4: ABS active 89% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T5: ABS active 72% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T1: usually 1.4 m wider at the apex than your best lap
findings.detail: Turning in too early or carrying too much speed pushes you away from the apex. Turn in a little later and aim to clip the inside kerb.

setup.title: Understeer on corner entry
setup.detail: Try trail braking deeper first (a driving fix). Setup options: move brake bias 1% rearward, soften front bump/rebound damping, or soften the front bar.

setup.title: Front wheels locking
setup.detail: Move brake bias 1-2% rearward (telemetry reads 40%; check the garage value), or reduce brake pressure slightly.

setup.title: RL: inside only 1.5°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RR: inside only -0.6°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 4 of 5 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T3, T4, T5. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 5 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 75.6% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

pros.title: Consistent through T2
pros.detail: Your section times there barely change from pass to pass, so you have found a repeatable approach.

cons.title: Coasting: 10.7% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 162 m per lap in T1, T2, T3, T4, T5. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 5 corners
cons.detail: In T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 ABS is active for 89% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 2 corners
cons.detail: T3, T4. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Wheels locking (T2, T3, T4, T5)
cons.detail: Locked wheels don't steer and flat-spot the tyre.

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T1)
cons.detail: T1: 1.4 m wider than your best lap. Missing the apex makes the corner longer and slower.

cons.title: Early apex (T3)
cons.detail: You cut to the inside too soon, then run wide on exit and have to wait before full throttle.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T2, T5)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T3, T4, T5
cons.detail: T3: 1.04 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.33 s between your average and best pass; T5: 0.31 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T3, T1.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit the brake hard first, and the moment ABS starts working, ease off 5-10% instead of holding the pedal down.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T1, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Keeping full brake pressure as speed drops
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as the car slows.

stopDoing.title: Turning in too early
stopDoing.detail: In T3, wait a beat longer before turning so the apex comes later and the exit is straighter.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (10.7% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Let AMS2 set steering lock for each car, and watch the FFB meter for clipping.

traits.name: Speed
traits.text: Quick. Braking points come up fast.

traits.name: Cornering grip
traits.text: Low grip: the car slides early, so be smooth and patient.

traits.name: Downforce
traits.text: No downforce: grip is the same at any speed.

traits.name: How forgiving
traits.text: Forgiving; a good car to learn in.

tips: Low grip: brake in a straight line, turn smoothly, and avoid sudden inputs.
